summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with acute epigastric and left upper quadrant abdominal pain, different in character from his usual anginal symptoms. Initial evaluation ruled out cardiac ischemia with normal ECG and negative troponins. CT abdomen showed no acute intra-abdominal pathology, normal mesenteric vessels, and no evidence of bowel ischemia or diverticulitis. The working diagnosis became diabetic gastroparesis given the postprandial pain, early satiety, and long-standing type 2 diabetes. His insulin regimen was adjusted during admission due to poor oral intake, and metformin was held due to elevated lactate. Chronic microcytic anemia was noted, with iron studies suggesting iron deficiency; outpatient evaluation for occult malignancy was recommended. The patient improved symptomatically and was discharged home with instructions to start iron supplementation, continue cardiac and diabetes medications, and follow up with GI for a gastric emptying study.
